title.zh: 卷十六 梁書16: 列傳六 葛從周 謝彥章 胡真 張歸霸 張歸厚 張歸弁
title.en: Volume 16 Book of Later Liang 16: Biographies 6 - Ge Congzhou, Xie Yanzhang, He Zhen, Zhang Guiba, Zhang Guihou, Zhang Guibian
title.raw: 卷十六 梁書16: 列傳六 葛從周 謝彥章 胡真 張歸霸 張歸厚 張歸弁 Volume 16 Book of Later Liang 16: Biographies 6 - Ge Congzhou, Xie Yanzhang, He Zhen, Zhang Guiba, Zhang Guihou, Zhang Guibian

sentences.zh: 葛從周，字通美，濮州鄄城人也。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou, style name Tongmei, was a native of Juancheng in Pu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou, styled Tongmei, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖阮，祖遇賢，父簡，累贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Ruan, grandfather Yu Xian, father Jian—repeatedly posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His line reached posthumous Minister of War through his father Jian.

sentences.zh: 從周少豁達，有智略，初入黃巢軍，漸至軍校。

translations.literal: Congzhou in youth was open and generous, had wisdom and stratagem; he first entered Huang Chao's army and gradually reached guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Open and shrewd in youth, he joined Huang Chao and rose to guard officer.

sentences.zh: 唐中和四年三月，太祖大破巢軍於王滿渡，從周與霍存、張歸霸昆弟相率來降。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Zhonghe of Tang the Founder greatly defeated Chao's army at Wangman Ford; Congzhou with Huo Cun and Zhang Guiba and his brothers in succession came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhonghe 4, month 3, after the Founder crushed Chao at Wangman Ford, Congzhou surrendered with Huo Cun and the Zhang brothers.

sentences.zh: 七月，從太祖屯兵於西華，破蔡賊王夏寨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Founder encamped troops at Xihua and broke Cai bandit Wang Xia's stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Month 7 he camped at Xihua and broke Cai rebel Wang Xia's camp.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨陣馬踣，賊眾來追甚急，從周扶太祖上馬，與賊軍格鬥，傷面，矢中於肱，身被數槍，奮命以衛太祖。

translations.literal: The Founder in battle his horse fell; bandit masses came pressing in pursuit very urgently; Congzhou helped the Founder mount, grappled with the bandit army, wounded his face, an arrow struck his upper arm, his body received several spears, and he exhausted his life to guard the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder's horse fell under pursuit, Congzhou mounted him, fought on wounded by face, arm, and spears, and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 賴張延壽回馬轉鬥，從周與太祖俱免，退軍溵水。

translations.literal: Relying on Zhang Yanshou wheeling his horse and turning to fight, Congzhou and the Founder both escaped; the army withdrew to Yin River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshou's countercharge let Congzhou and the Founder escape to Yin River.

sentences.zh: 諸將並削職，惟擢從周、延壽為大校。

translations.literal: The generals all had offices reduced; only Congzhou and Yanshou were promoted to great colonels.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals were demoted; only Congzhou and Yanshou were promoted.

sentences.zh: 其從入長葛、靈井，大敗蔡賊，至斤溝、淝河，殺鐵林三千人，獲九寨都虞候王涓。

translations.literal: Following in to enter Changge and Lingjing, he greatly defeated Cai bandits; reaching Jingou and Fei River he killed three thousand Iron Forest troops and captured nine-stockade commander Wang Juan.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Changge and Lingjing, killed three thousand Iron Forest troops at Fei River, and captured commander Wang Juan.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣郭言募兵於陝州，有黃花子賊據於溫穀，從周擊破之。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Guo Yan to recruit troops at Shan prefecture; Yellow Flower bandits held Wengu; Congzhou broke and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the Yellow Flower bandits at Wengu while Guo Yan recruited at Shan.

sentences.zh: 又破秦賢之眾於滎陽，尋佐朱珍收兵於淄、青間。

translations.literal: He again defeated Qin Xian's masses at Xingyang and soon aided Zhu Zhen in gathering troops between Zi and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Qin Xian at Xingyang and aided Zhu Zhen in Zi and Qing.

sentences.zh: 時兗州齊克護軍於任城，從周敗之，擒其將呂全真。

translations.literal: At that time Yanzhou's Qi Kerang had troops at Rencheng; Congzhou defeated him and captured his general Lü Quanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Qi Kerang at Rencheng and captured Lü Quanzhen.

sentences.zh: 淄人不受制，復與之戰，獲其驍將鞏約。

translations.literal: Zi people would not submit; he fought them again and took their fierce general Gong Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi resisted he fought again and took the fierce Gong Yue.

sentences.zh: 會青州以步騎萬餘人列三寨於金嶺，以厄要害，從周與朱珍大殲其眾，擄其將楊昭範五人而還。

translations.literal: When Qing prefecture with more than ten thousand foot and horse arrayed three stockades at Jin Ridge to choke the crucial point, Congzhou with Zhu Zhen greatly annihilated their masses, captured their general Yang Zhaofan and five men, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhu Zhen annihilated Qing troops at Jin Ridge and captured Yang Zhaofan and five generals.

sentences.zh: 至大梁，不解甲，徑至板橋擊蔡賊，破盧瑭寨；

translations.literal: Reaching Daliang, not doffing armor, he went straight to Banqiao to strike Cai bandits and broke Lu Tang's stockade;
translations.idiomatic: Without resting at Daliang he struck Cai at Banqiao and broke Lu Tang's camp;

sentences.zh: 瑭自溺而死，又於赤岡殺蔡軍二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Tang drowned himself; again at Red Mound he killed more than twenty thousand Cai troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tang drowned; at Red Mound he killed twenty thousand Cai troops.

sentences.zh: 從討謝殷於亳州，擒之。

translations.literal: Following in the attack on Xie Yin at Bozhou, he captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Xie Yin at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 回襲曹州，擄刺史丘宏禮以歸。

translations.literal: Returning to raid Cao prefecture he captured military commissioner Qiu Hongli and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Raiding Cao he took commissioner Qiu Hongli.

sentences.zh: 與兗、鄆軍遇於臨濮之劉橋，殺數萬人，朱瑄、朱瑾僅以身免，擒都將鄒務卿已下五十人。

translations.literal: Meeting Yan and Yanzhou troops at Liu Bridge in Linpu he killed tens of thousands; Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin barely escaped with their bodies; he captured commander Zou Wuqing and below fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu Bridge he killed tens of thousands; Zhu Xuan and Jin barely escaped; he took fifty officers including Zou Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 從太祖至範縣，復與朱瑄戰，擄尹萬榮等三人，遂平濮州。

translations.literal: Following the Founder to Fan county he again fought Zhu Xuan, captured Yin Wanrong and three others, and then pacified Pu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Fan he beat Zhu Xuan, took Yin Wanrong and others, and pacified Pu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與朱珍擊蔡賊於陳、亳間，獲都將石璠。

translations.literal: Before long with Zhu Zhen he struck Cai bandits between Chen and Bo and captured commander Shi Fan.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhu Zhen he beat Cai between Chen and Bo and took Shi Fan.

sentences.zh: 文德元年，魏博軍亂，樂從訓來告急，從太祖渡河，拔黎陽、李固、臨河等鎮，至內黃，破魏軍萬餘眾，獲其將周儒等十人。

translations.literal: In Wende year 1 Wei-Bo army mutinied; Le Congxun came reporting urgent distress; following the Founder across the river he took Li Yang, Liguo, Linhe, and other posts; reaching Neihuang he broke more than ten thousand Wei troops and captured their generals Zhou Ru and ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Wende 1 he crossed the river with the Founder, took Li Yang and other posts, and at Neihuang captured Zhou Ru and ten Wei officers.

sentences.zh: 李罕之引並人圍張全義於河陽，從周與丁會、張存敬、牛存節率兵赴援，大破並軍，殺蕃漢二萬人，解河陽之圍，以功表授檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi led Jin men to besiege Zhang Quanyi at Heyang; Congzhou with Ding Hui, Zhang Cunjing, and Niu Cunjie led troops to the rescue, greatly defeated Jin troops, killed twenty thousand Han and barbarian, lifted Heyang's siege, and for merit was memorialized honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Heyang from Li Hanzhi's Jin siege, killed twenty thousand, and became honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 從朱珍討徐州，撥豐縣，敗時溥於吳康，得其輜重，加檢校刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Following Zhu Zhen to attack Xuzhou he took Feng county, defeated Shi Pu at Wukang, obtained his baggage train, and was added honorary Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou he took Feng, beat Shi Pu at Wukang, and became honorary Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 佐龐師古討孫儒於淮南，略地至廬、壽、滁等州，下天長、高郵，破邵伯堰。

translations.literal: Aiding Pang Shigu against Sun Ru in Huainan he swept territory to Lu, Shou, and Chu prefectures, took Tianchang and Gaoyou, and broke Shaobo Dam.
translations.idiomatic: In Huainan with Pang Shigu he took Lu, Shou, Chu, Tianchang, and Gaoyou and broke Shaobo Dam.

sentences.zh: 回軍攻濠州，殺刺史魏勳，得餉船十艘。

translations.literal: Returning he attacked Haozhou, killed military commissioner Wei Xun, and obtained ten supply boats.
translations.idiomatic: He took Haozhou, killed Wei Xun, and seized ten supply boats.

sentences.zh: 大順元年八月，並帥圍潞州，太祖遣從周率敢死之士，夜銜枚犯圍而入，會王師不利於馬牢川，即棄上黨而歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Datong year 1 Jin commander besieged Lu prefecture; the Founder sent Congzhou with dare-death troops who by night held branches in their mouths and broke through the encirclement to enter; when the royal army was unfavorable at Malaichuan he then abandoned Shangdang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Datong 1, month 8, he slipped into besieged Lu; after defeat at Malaichuan the army abandoned Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，與丁會諸將討魏州，連收十邑。

translations.literal: That year, twelfth month, with Ding Hui and generals he attacked Wei prefecture and in succession took ten districts.
translations.idiomatic: Month 12 he and Ding Hui took ten Wei districts.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，大破魏軍於永定橋，魏軍五敗，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: The next year, first month, he greatly defeated Wei troops at Yongding Bridge; Wei army five defeats, beheading more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Month 1 next year he routed Wei five times at Yongding Bridge with ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 十月，佐丁會攻宿州，從周壅水灌其城，刺史張筠以郡降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month aiding Ding Hui in attacking Suzhou, Congzhou dammed water to flood the city; military commissioner Zhang Yun surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Month 10 he flooded Suzhou and Zhang Yun surrendered.

sentences.zh: 從討兗州，破朱瑾之軍於馬溝。

translations.literal: Following in the attack on Yanzhou he broke Zhu Jin's army at Magou.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Zhu Jin at Magou in the Yanzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 景福二年二月，與諸將大破徐、兗之兵於石佛山。

translations.literal: In the second month of Jingfu year 2 with generals he greatly defeated Xu and Yanzhou troops at Stone Buddha Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfu 2, month 2, he crushed Xu and Yan troops at Stone Buddha Mountain.

sentences.zh: 八月，與龐師古同攻兗州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month with Pang Shigu he jointly attacked Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Month 8 he besieged Yanzhou with Pang Shigu.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年三月，軍至新泰縣，朱瑾令都將張約、李胡椒率三千人來拒戰，師古遣從周、張存敬掩襲，生擒張約、李胡椒等都將數十人。

translations.literal: In the third month of Qianning year 1 the army reached Xintai county; Zhu Jin ordered commander Zhang Yue and Li Hujiao to lead three thousand men to resist; Shigu sent Congzhou and Zhang Cunjing in ambush strike and captured Zhang Yue, Li Hujiao, and several tens of commanders alive.
translations.idiomatic: Qianning 1, month 3, he ambushed and captured Zhang Yue, Li Hujiao, and dozens of Yan officers at Xintai.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，圍兗州，兗人不出，從周詐揚言並人、鄆人來救，即引軍趨高吳，夜半卻潛歸寨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of year 2 besieging Yanzhou, Yan people did not come out; Congzhou falsely proclaimed Jin and Yanzhou men coming to rescue, then led troops toward Gaowu; at midnight he secretly returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Yan he feigned a Jin-Yan relief march, then doubled back at night.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾果出兵攻外壕，我軍士突出，掩殺千餘人，生擒都將張漢筠。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin indeed sent troops to attack the outer moat; our soldiers burst out, ambushed and killed more than a thousand, and captured commander Zhang Hanyun alive.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sallied; Congzhou ambushed and killed a thousand and captured Zhang Hanyun.

sentences.zh: 從周累立戰功，自懷州刺史曆曹、宿二州刺史，累遷檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: Congzhou repeatedly established battle merit; from Huai prefecture military commissioner he passed through Cao and Su prefecture military commissioners, repeatedly rising to honorary Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Huai to Cao and Su commissioner to honorary Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，並帥以大軍侵魏，遣其子落落率二千騎屯洹水，從周以馬步二千人擊之，殺戮殆盡，擒落落於陣，並帥號泣而去。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year 3 the Jin commander with a great army invaded Wei and sent his son Luoluo with two thousand cavalry to camp at Huan River; Congzhou with two thousand horse and foot struck them, slaughter nearly all, and captured Luoluo in the formation; the Jin commander wailed and left.
translations.idiomatic: Month 5, year 3, he destroyed Luoluo's two thousand cavalry at Huan River and captured Keyong's son.

sentences.zh: 遂自洹水與龐師古渡河擊鄆。

translations.literal: He then from Huan River with Pang Shigu crossed the river to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed from Huan with Pang Shigu to attack Yan.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，下之。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 4 he took it.
translations.idiomatic: Month 1, year 4, Yan fell.

sentences.zh: 從周乘勝伐兗，會朱瑾出師在徐境，其將康懷英以城降。

translations.literal: Congzhou took victory in stride to attack Yan; when Zhu Jin marched out on campaign in Xu territory his general Kang Huaiying surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing Yan he took it when Kang Huaiying surrendered while Jin was away.

sentences.zh: 以功授兗州留後、檢校司空。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Yanzhou acting commissioner and honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He became Yan acting commissioner and honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 復領兵萬餘人渡淮討楊行密，至濠州，聞龐師古清口之敗，遽班師。

translations.literal: Again he led more than ten thousand troops across the Huai to attack Yang Xingmi; reaching Haozhou he heard of Pang Shigu's defeat at Qingkou and hastily withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Huai against Yang Xingmi he withdrew on news of Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 光化元年四月，率師經略山東，時並帥以大軍屯邢、洺，從周至钜鹿與並軍遇，大破之，並帥遁走。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Guanghua year 1 he led troops to pacify Shandong; at that time the Jin commander with a great army camped at Xing and Ming; Congzhou at Julu met Jin troops and greatly defeated them; the Jin commander fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua 1, month 4, he routed the Jin army at Julu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 我軍追襲至青山口，數日之內，邢、洺、磁三州連下，斬首二萬級，獲將吏一百五十人，即以從周兼領邢州留後。

translations.literal: Our army pursued to Qingshan Pass; within several days Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures fell in succession; beheading twenty thousand, capturing a hundred fifty officers and clerks; Congzhou was made concurrent Xingzhou acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued to Qingshan and took Xing, Ming, and Ci with twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 十月，復破並軍五千騎於張公橋。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he again defeated five thousand Jin cavalry at Zhanggong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Month 10 he beat five thousand Jin horse at Zhanggong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 晉將李嗣昭急攻邢州，陣於城門外，從周大破之，擒蕃將賁金鐵、慕容騰百餘人。

translations.literal: Jin general Li Sizhao urgently attacked Xingzhou, arrayed outside the city gate; Congzhou greatly defeated him and captured more than a hundred barbarian generals Ben Jintie and Murong Teng.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed Li Sizhao at Xingzhou and captured a hundred Jin officers.

sentences.zh: 二年春，幽州劉仁恭率軍十萬寇魏州，屠貝郡。

translations.literal: In spring of year 2 Youzhou's Liu Rengong led a hundred thousand army to raid Wei prefecture and slaughter Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Spring year 2 Liu Rengong ravaged Wei and slaughtered Bei.

sentences.zh: 從周自邢台馳入魏州，燕軍突上水關，攻館陶門。

translations.literal: Congzhou from Xingtai galloped into Wei prefecture; Yan army suddenly rushed the upper water gate and attacked Guantao Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped from Xingtai as Yan stormed Guantao Gate.

sentences.zh: 從周與賀德倫率五百騎出戰，謂門者曰：「前有敵，不可返顧！

translations.literal: Congzhou with He Delun led five hundred cavalry out to battle and told the gatekeepers: "Enemies ahead—you must not look back!"
translations.idiomatic: With He Delun he charged out crying, "Enemies ahead—do not turn back!"

sentences.zh: 」命闔其門。

translations.literal: " He ordered the gates shut.
translations.idiomatic: He had the gates shut.

sentences.zh: 從周等極力死戰，大敗燕人，擒都將薛突厥、王郃郎等。

translations.literal: Congzhou and the rest exhausted strength in death battle, greatly defeated Yan men, and captured commanders Xue Tujue and Wang Helang and others.
translations.idiomatic: They fought to the death and captured Xue Tujue and Wang Helang.

sentences.zh: 翌日，破其八寨，追擊至臨清，劉仁恭走滄州，從周授宣義軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: The next day he broke their eight stockades, pursued to Linqing; Liu Rengong fled to Cangzhou; Congzhou was appointed Xuanyi army campaign deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he broke eight camps, pursued to Linqing, and Rengong fled to Cang.

sentences.zh: 五月，並人討李罕之於潞州，太祖以丁會代罕之，令從周馳入上黨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jin men attacked Li Hanzhi at Lu prefecture; the Founder made Ding Hui replace Hanzhi and ordered Congzhou to gallop into Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Month 5 he galloped into Shangdang as Jin attacked Lu.

sentences.zh: 七月，並人陷澤州，太祖召從周，令賀德倫守潞州，德倫等尋棄城而歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jin men took Ze prefecture; the Founder summoned Congzhou and ordered He Delun to guard Lu prefecture; Delun and the rest soon abandoned the city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Month 7 Ze fell; He Delun abandoned Lu despite orders.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，領軍討滄州，先攻德州，下之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of year 3 he led troops to attack Cangzhou, first attacking De prefecture and taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Month 4, year 3, he took De then marched on Cang.

sentences.zh: 及進攻浮陽，幽州劉仁恭大舉來援。

translations.literal: When advancing to attack Fuyang, Youzhou's Liu Rengong came in great force to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Fuyang he faced Liu Rengong's great relief army.

sentences.zh: 時都監蔣元暉謂諸將曰：「吾王命我護軍，志在攻取，今燕帥來赴，不可外戰，當縱其入壁，聚食囷廩，力屈糧盡，必可取也。

translations.literal: At that time overseer Jiang Yuanhui told the generals: "Our prince ordered me to protect the army with intent to attack and take; now the Yan commander comes to the rescue—we cannot fight outside; we should let them enter the walls, gather and eat from granaries, and when strength is spent and grain exhausted they can surely be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Overseer Jiang Yuanhui urged letting Rengong in to starve him; Congzhou disagreed.

sentences.zh: 」從周對曰：「兵在機，機在上將，非督護所言也。

translations.literal: Congzhou replied: "War lies in opportunity; opportunity lies in the chief general—not what the overseer says."
translations.idiomatic: "War is the general's call, not the overseer's," Congzhou said.

sentences.zh: 」乃令張存敬、氏叔琮守其寨。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Zhang Cunjing and Shi Shuzong to guard the stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He left Zhang Cunjing and Shi Shuzong to hold camp.

sentences.zh: 從周逆戰於乾寧軍老鴉堤，大破燕軍，斬首三萬，獲將佐馬慎交已下百餘人，奪馬三千匹。

translations.literal: Congzhou met battle at Qianning army Old Crow Embankment, greatly defeated Yan army, beheaded thirty thousand, captured generals and aides Ma Shenjiao and below a hundred men, and seized three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: At Old Crow Embankment he killed thirty thousand Yan troops and took three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 八月，並人攻邢、洺，從太祖破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Jin men attacked Xing and Ming; following the Founder he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Month 8 he beat Jin at Xing and Ming with the Founder.

sentences.zh: 從周追襲至青山口，斬首五千級，獲其將王郃郎、楊師悅等，得馬千匹，表授檢校太保，兼徐州兩使留後，尋為兗州節度使。

translations.literal: Congzhou pursued to Qingshan Pass, beheaded five thousand, captured their generals Wang Helang, Yang Shiyue, and others, obtained a thousand horses, was memorialized honorary Grand Guardian, concurrent Xu two-circuits acting commissioner, soon Yanzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Qingshan he took five thousand heads and became Yan commissioner and honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 謝彥章，許州人。

translations.literal: Xie Yanzhang was a Xu prefecture man.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yanzhang came from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼事從周為養父，從周憐其敏慧，教以兵法，常以千錢於大盤中，布其行陣偏伍之狀，示以出沒進退之節，彥章盡得其訣。

translations.literal: In youth he served Congzhou as adopted father; Congzhou pitied his quick intelligence, taught him military arts, often used a thousand cash on a great tray to array battle formations and partial units, showing advance-and-retreat rhythm; Yanzhang fully obtained the secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted by Congzhou, he learned warfare on a tray of coins modeling formations.

sentences.zh: 及壯，事太祖為騎將。

translations.literal: When grown he served the Founder as a cavalry officer.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he served the Founder as cavalry officer.

sentences.zh: 末帝嗣位，用為兩京馬軍都軍使，累與晉軍接戰有功，尋領河陽節度使。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, he was used as both-capitals horse army overall commander; repeatedly fighting Jin troops he had merit; soon he held Heyang military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he commanded both capitals' cavalry, won against Jin, and became Heyang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及從周卒，臨喪行服，躬預葬事，時人義之。

translations.literal: When Congzhou died he attended the mourning wearing funeral garb and personally took part in burial; men of the time praised the righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned Congzhou in full filial rites and was praised.

sentences.zh: 彥章後為許州節度使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Yanzhang later was Xu military commissioner and honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Xu commissioner and honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 貞明四年冬，滑州節度使賀瑰為北面招討使，彥章為排陣使，同領大軍，駐於行台寨，與晉人對壘。

translations.literal: In winter of Zhenming year 4 Huazhou military commissioner He Gui was northern campaign commander; Yanzhang was array commander; together they led the great army, camped at Xingtai Stockade, and faced Jin men in opposing camps.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenming 4 winter he and He Gui camped at Xingtai against the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 彥章時領騎軍與之挑戰，晉人或望我軍行陣整肅，則相謂曰：「必兩京太傅在此也。

translations.literal: Yanzhang then led cavalry to challenge them; Jin men sometimes seeing our army's formations neat and stern would say to one another: "The two-capitals Grand Tutor must be here."
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops feared his cavalry and said, "The Grand Tutor must be here."

sentences.zh: 」不敢以名呼，其為敵人所憚如此。

translations.literal: They did not dare call him by name; such was the enemy's fear of him.
translations.idiomatic: They would not speak his name aloud.

sentences.zh: 是時咸謂賀瑰能將步軍，彥章能領騎士，既名聲相軋，故瑰心忌之。

translations.literal: At that time all said He Gui could command foot soldiers and Yanzhang could lead cavalry; since fame rubbed against each other, Gui therefore resented him in heart.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui resented Yanzhang because both were famed commanders.

sentences.zh: 一日，與瑰同設伏於郊外，瑰指一方地謂彥章曰：「此地岡阜隆起，中央坦夷，好列柵之所。

translations.literal: One day with Gui he jointly set ambush in the suburbs; Gui pointed at one plot of ground and told Yanzhang: "This place's mound rises and the center is level—good for setting palisades."
translations.idiomatic: Gui showed him a hill and said it was ideal for palisades.

sentences.zh: 」尋而晉人舍之，故瑰疑彥章與晉人通；

translations.literal: Soon Jin men abandoned it; therefore Gui suspected Yanzhang communicated with Jin men;
translations.idiomatic: Jin avoided it; Gui suspected Yanzhang of collusion;

sentences.zh: 又瑰欲速戰，彥章欲持重以老敵人，瑰益疑之。

translations.literal: Again Gui wished swift battle; Yanzhang wished to hold weight and wear out the enemy; Gui's suspicion increased.
translations.idiomatic: Gui wanted battle; Yanzhang wanted delay; suspicion grew.

sentences.zh: 會為行營馬步都虞候朱珪所誣，瑰遂與珪邦協謀，因享士伏甲以殺彥章及濮州刺史孟審澄、別將侯溫裕等於軍，以謀叛聞。

translations.literal: When camp horse-and-foot chief commandant Zhu Gui slandered him, Gui then with Gui conspired, and at a feast for officers set hidden armor and killed Yanzhang, Bozhou military commissioner Meng Shencheng, and separate commander Hou Wenyu and others in the army, reporting it as plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui slandered him; at a feast Gui ambushed and killed Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, and Hou Wenyu as traitors.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞之，喜曰：「彼將帥如是，亡無日矣。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin heard it and said with pleasure: "Their generals like this—ruin will come in no long day."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin rejoiced, "With generals like that they will soon fall."

sentences.zh: 審澄、溫裕亦善將騎軍，然所領不過三千騎；

translations.literal: Shencheng and Wenyu were also good at commanding cavalry, yet their commands did not exceed three thousand horse;
translations.idiomatic: Shencheng and Wenyu led only three thousand horse;

sentences.zh: 多而益辦，惟彥章有焉。

translations.literal: many yet more able—only Yanzhang had it.
translations.idiomatic: only Yanzhang commanded more with equal skill.

sentences.zh: 將略之外，好優禮儒士。

translations.literal: Beyond generalship he loved to honor Ruist gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond tactics he honored scholars.

sentences.zh: 與晉人對壘於河上，恒褒衣博帶，動皆由禮，或臨敵禦眾，則肅然有上將之威。

translations.literal: Facing Jin men in opposing camps on the river he always wore loose robes and broad belt; every movement followed ritual; sometimes facing the enemy controlling the masses he was stern with a great commander's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the river he wore scholar's robes yet showed a commander's stern majesty in battle.

sentences.zh: 每敦陣整旅，左旋右抽，雖風馳雨驟，亦無以喻其迅捷也，故當時騎士鹹樂為用。

translations.literal: Each time he arrayed ranks and regulated brigades, wheeling left and striking right—even wind gallop and rain burst could not compare to his swiftness; therefore cavalrymen of the time all delighted to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: His cavalry maneuvers were swifter than storm; horsemen loved to follow him.

sentences.zh: 及其遇害，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: When he met harm people all mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: His murder was widely mourned.

sentences.zh: 胡真，江陵人也。

translations.literal: Hu Zhen was a Jiangling man.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhen came from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 體貌洪壯，長七尺，善騎射，少為縣吏。

translations.literal: His physique was huge and strong, seven feet tall, skilled at mounted archery; in youth he was a county clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Seven feet tall and a master archer, he began as a county clerk.

sentences.zh: 及在巢寇中，寇推為名將，隨巢涉淮、浙，陷許、洛，入長安。

translations.literal: When in Chao's banditry the bandits pushed him as a famous general; he followed Chao across Huai and Zhe, took Xu and Luo, and entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Huang Chao's ranks he became a famed general and entered Chang'an with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 及太祖以眾歸唐，真時為元從都將，

translations.literal: When the Founder with masses returned to Tang, Zhen was then original-follower overall commander,
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder submitted to Tang, Zhen was an original-follower commander,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Zhu Quanzhong and Hu Zhen:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Zhu Quanzhong and Hu Zhen:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》云：溫見巢兵勢日蹙，知其將亡，親將胡真、謝瞳勸溫歸國。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Zhu saw Chao's military power daily pinched, knew he would perish, and personally led Hu Zhen and Xie Tong to urge Zhu to return to the state.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Zhu Quanzhong urged return to Tang with Hu Zhen and Xie Tong.)〉

sentences.zh: 從至梁苑，表授檢校刑部尚書，頻從破巢、蔡於陳、鄭間。

translations.literal: Following to Liang Garden he was memorialized honorary Minister of Punishments and repeatedly followed in breaking Chao and Cai between Chen and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang Garden he became honorary Minister of Punishments and fought Chao and Cai.

sentences.zh: 尋以奇兵襲取滑州，乃署為滑州節度留後，復表為鄭滑節度使、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Soon with strange troops he raided and took Huazhou and was appointed Huazhou military acting commissioner; again memorialized Zheng-Hua military commissioner and honorary Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Huazhou and became Zheng-Hua commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數年，征為右金吾衛大將軍，俄拜寧遠軍節度使、容州刺史、檢校太保。

translations.literal: After several years he was summoned as Right Golden Guard great general; soon he was made Ningyuan army military commissioner, Rong prefecture military commissioner, and honorary Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Golden Guard general, then Ningyuan and Rong commissioner and honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 卒贈太傅。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 張歸霸，字正臣，清河人。

translations.literal: Zhang Guiba, style name Zhengchen, was a Qinghe man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guiba, styled Zhengchen, came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖進言，陽穀令。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jinyan was Yanggu county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jinyan was magistrate of Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 父實，亦有宦緒。

translations.literal: Father Shi also had an official pedigree.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi also held office.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，好兵術。

translations.literal: In youth he was unconventional, loved military arts.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was bold and loved warfare.

sentences.zh: 唐乾符中，寇盜蜂起，歸霸率昆弟三人棄家投黃巢，頗以勇略聞。

translations.literal: In Qianfu of Tang bandits and robbers swarmed; Guiba led three brothers to abandon home and join Huang Chao, quite known for courage and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu he and three brothers joined Huang Chao for their fighting fame.

sentences.zh: 巢陷長安，遂署為左番功臣。

translations.literal: When Chao took Chang'an he was appointed Left Merit Baron.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao took Chang'an he became Left Merit Baron.

sentences.zh: 中和中，巢領徒走宛丘。

translations.literal: In Zhonghe, Chao led followers to flee to Wankiu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhonghe Chao fled to Wankiu.

sentences.zh: 時太祖在汴，奉詔南討，巢黨日窘，歸霸昆仲與葛從周、李讜等相率來降，尋補宣武軍劇職。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder was at Bian, received edict for southern campaign; Chao's party daily pressed; Guiba and his brothers with Ge Congzhou, Li Rang, and others in succession came to surrender; soon he was supplemented to Xuanyi army key posts.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian Guiba and his brothers surrendered with Congzhou and Li Rang and joined the Xuanyi army.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，與蔡將張存戰於盧氏。

translations.literal: In Guangqi year 2 he fought Cai general Zhang Cun at Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi 2 he fought Zhang Cun at Lushi.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，又與蔡將盧瑭戰於雙丘，復與秦宗賢戰於萬勝，皆敗而殲之。

translations.literal: In summer of year 3 he again fought Cai general Lu Tang at Shuangqiu and again fought Qin Zongxian at Wansheng—all defeated and annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3 summer he destroyed Lu Tang at Shuangqiu and Qin Zongxian at Wansheng.

sentences.zh: 翌日，宗權遣將張郅來寇，列寨於赤堈。

translations.literal: The next day Zongquan sent general Zhang Zhi to raid, arraying stockades at Chijin.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Zhang Zhi of Cai camped at Chijin.

sentences.zh: 一日，出騎將較勝，歸霸為飛戈所中。

translations.literal: One day he sent out cavalry to contest victory; Guiba was struck by a flying halberd.
translations.idiomatic: In a cavalry duel he was struck by a flying halberd.

sentences.zh: 即拔馬卻逸，控弦一發，賊洞頸而墜，遂兼騎而還。

translations.literal: He at once pulled his horse back and fled, drew his bow one shot—the bandit pierced through the neck and fell; he then took the horse and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled, shot the rider through the neck, and seized his horse.

sentences.zh: 太祖時於高丘下瞰，備見其狀，麵加賞激，厚以金帛及所獲馬錫之。

translations.literal: The Founder at that time overlooked from Gaomound and fully saw the scene; he added praise and stimulation to his face and richly bestowed gold silks and captured horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder watched from Gaomound and richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗被命以控弦之士五百人伏於壕內，太祖統數百騎稍逼其寨，蔡人果以銳士摩壘來追，歸霸發伏兵，掩殺千餘人，奪馬數十匹，尋奏授檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was also ordered with five hundred archers to lie in ambush in a trench; the Founder with several hundred horse slightly pressed their stockade; Cai men indeed with crack troops rubbed the ramparts in pursuit; Guiba released ambush troops, ambushed and killed more than a thousand, seized several tens of horses, and soon memorialized honorary Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His trench ambush killed a thousand Cai pursuers and won him honorary Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.

sentences.zh: 其後從太祖伐鄆，副李唐賓渡淮，鹹著奇績。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed the Founder in attacking Yan and as deputy to Li Tangbin crossed the Huai, all showing strange merit.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Huai with Li Tangbin against Yan with striking merit.

sentences.zh: 文德初，大軍臨蔡州，賊將蕭顥來斫寨，歸霸於徐懷玉各以所領兵自東南二扉分出，合勢殺賊，蔡人大敗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wende the great army approached Caizhou; bandit general Xiao Hao came to cut the stockade; Guiba with Xu Huaiyu each led their commands out from southeast and second gates, joined force and killed bandits; Cai men were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wende at Caizhou he and Xu Huaiyu sallied and crushed Xiao Hao.

sentences.zh: 及太祖振眾離營，寇塵已息。

translations.literal: When the Founder rallied the masses and left camp the bandit dust had already settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder left camp the field was already clear.

sentences.zh: 太祖召至，賞之曰：「昔耿弇不俟光武擊張步，言不以賊遺君父，弇之功，爾其二焉。

translations.literal: The Founder summoned him and rewarded him saying: "Formerly Geng Yan did not wait for Guangwu to strike Zhang Bu, saying he would not leave bandits to lord and father—Yan's merit, yours is twice it."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder compared him to Geng Yan, who would not leave rebels for his emperor.

sentences.zh: 」大順中，郭紹賓拔曹州，歸霸率兵數千守之。

translations.literal: In Datong, Guo Shaobin took Cao prefecture; Guiba led several thousand troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Datong he garrisoned Cao after Guo Shaobin took it.

sentences.zh: 俄而朱瑾統大軍自至，歸霸與丁會逆擊之於金鄉，瑾大敗，擒賊將宗江等七十餘人，曹州以寧。

translations.literal: Soon Zhu Jin led a great army in person; Guiba with Ding Hui met and struck them at Jinxiang; Jin was greatly defeated; bandit generals Zong Jiang and more than seventy men were captured; Cao prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ding Hui routed Zhu Jin at Jinxiang and captured seventy officers.

sentences.zh: 明年，破濮州，生擒刺史邵儒。

translations.literal: The next year he took Pu prefecture and captured military commissioner Shao Ru alive.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he took Pu and captured Shao Ru alive.

sentences.zh: 又佐葛從周與晉軍戰於洹水，生獲克用愛子落落。

translations.literal: He again aided Ge Congzhou in fighting Jin troops at Huan River and captured Keyong's beloved son Luoluo alive.
translations.idiomatic: At Huan River he helped capture Keyong's son Luoluo.

sentences.zh: 復與燕人戰於內黃，殺仁恭兵三萬餘眾。

translations.literal: He again fought Yan men at Neihuang and killed more than thirty thousand of Rengong's troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Neihuang he killed thirty thousand Yan troops.

sentences.zh: 戎績超特，居諸將之右，累官至檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: Military achievement exceptionally surpassing, he stood to the right of the generals, successively reaching honorary Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: His merit topped the generals; he reached honorary Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 光化二年，權知邢州事。

translations.literal: In Guanghua year 2 he was provisional Xingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua 2 he governed Xingzhou provisionally.

sentences.zh: 明年春，李嗣昭以蕃漢五萬來寇，歸霸堅壁設備，晉軍不敢顧其城，遂移軍攻洺州，陷焉。

translations.literal: The next spring Li Sizhao with fifty thousand Han and barbarian came to raid; Guiba fortified walls and set defenses; Jin troops did not dare look at the city and shifted army to attack Ming prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring he held Xingzhou while Sizhao bypassed it and took Ming.

sentences.zh: 時太祖在滑，頗慮邢之失守。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder was at Hua and quite feared Xing's loss.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder at Hua feared Xing would fall.

sentences.zh: 及葛從周復洺，嗣昭北遁，歸霸出兵襲之，殺二萬餘眾。

translations.literal: When Ge Congzhou recovered Ming, Sizhao fled north; Guiba led troops in ambush strike and killed more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Congzhou retook Ming, Guiba ambushed Sizhao and killed twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 捷至，賞錫殊等，旋以功奏加檢校司空。

translations.literal: Victory arrived; rewards and gifts were special; soon for merit memorialized added honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was richly rewarded and made honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，遷萊州刺史，秩滿授左衛上將軍，又除曹州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was transferred Laizhou prefect; when term expired he was appointed Left Guard upper general; again made Cao prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianyou he governed Lai, then became Left Guard general and Cao commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其秋，加檢校司徒，副劉知俊禦邠、鳳之寇，敗之。

translations.literal: That autumn he was added honorary Minister of Works, deputy to Liu Zhijun in resisting Bin and Feng raiders, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he helped Liu Zhijun beat Bin and Feng raiders.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，拜右龍虎統軍，改左驍衛上將軍，充河陽諸軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was made Right Dragon-Tiger overall commander, changed to Left Valiant Guard upper general, full Heyang all-armies overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication he commanded dragon-tiger and valiant guard troops and Heyang armies.

sentences.zh: 明年夏六月，就除河陽節度使、檢校太保，尋加同平章事。

translations.literal: The next summer, sixth month, he was appointed Heyang military commissioner and honorary Grand Guardian; soon added co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Next summer he became Heyang commissioner, Grand Guardian, and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 二年秋七月，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn of year 2 he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2, autumn, month 7, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太傅。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝德妃張氏，即歸霸女也。

translations.literal: Liang Last Emperor Virtuous Consort Zhang was Guiba's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor's Virtuous Consort Zhang was his daughter.

sentences.zh: 末帝嗣位，以歸霸子漢鼎、漢傑並為近職。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Guiba's sons Handing and Hanjie were both made close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Handing and Hanjie became palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 漢鼎早亡，漢傑貞明中為控鶴指揮使，領兵討惠王於陳州，擒之。

translations.literal: Handing died early; in Zhenming Hanjie was Crane-Control commander, led troops to attack Prince of Hui at Chenzhou, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjie captured the Prince of Hui at Chen in Zhenming.

sentences.zh: 當貞明、龍德之際，漢傑昆仲分掌權要，藩鎮除拜多出其門，段凝因之遂竊兵柄。

translations.literal: During Zhenming and Longde, the Hanjie brothers in turn held crucial power; frontier appointments mostly came from their gate; Duan Ning therefore stole military authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanjie brothers dominated appointments until Duan Ning seized the army.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗入汴，漢傑與兄漢倫、弟漢融同日伏誅於汴橋下。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Hanjie with elder brother Hanlun and younger brother Hanrong on the same day were executed at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took Bian the three brothers were executed at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 張歸厚，字德坤，

translations.literal: Zhang Guihou, style name Dekun,
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guihou, styled Dekun,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Guihou's ancestry:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Guihou's ancestry:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒考異》引《梁功臣列傳》云：歸厚祖興，父處讓。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Mirror Examined》 cites the 《Biographies of Liang Merit Ministers》: Guihou's grandfather Xing, father Churang.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Mirror Examined》 supplement cites the 《Biographies of Liang Merit Ministers》: grandfather Xing, father Churang.)〉

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，有機略，尤長於弓槊之用。

translations.literal: In youth fierce and brave, had resourcefulness, especially excelled in bow and spear use.
translations.idiomatic: Young he was fierce, clever, and master of bow and spear.

sentences.zh: 中和末，與兄歸霸自巢軍相率來降，太祖署為軍校。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhonghe with elder brother Guiba he came from Chao's army in succession to surrender; the Founder appointed him army officer.
translations.idiomatic: Late Zhonghe he surrendered from Chao with Guiba as army officer.

sentences.zh: 時淮西兵力方壯，太祖之師尚寡，歸厚以少擊眾，往無不捷。

translations.literal: At that time Huaixi military power was just strong; the Founder's army was still few; Guihou with few struck many and went nowhere without victory.
translations.idiomatic: Though few against many, he never lost.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年春，與秦宗賢戰於萬勝，大破之。

translations.literal: In spring of Guangqi year 3 he fought Qin Zongxian at Wansheng and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi 3 spring he crushed Qin Zongxian at Wansheng.

sentences.zh: 其夏，蔡將張至以數萬眾屯於赤堈，歸厚嘗與至單騎鬥於陣，至不能支而奔，師徒乘此大捷。

translations.literal: That summer Cai general Zhang Zhi with tens of thousands encamped at Chijin; Guihou once single-horse dueled Zhi in the formation; Zhi could not sustain and fled; the army took this great victory.
translations.idiomatic: He single-handedly drove off Zhang Zhi at Chijin in a mounted duel.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，立署為騎軍長，仍以鞍馬器幣錫之。

translations.literal: The Founder was greatly pleased, immediately appointed him cavalry army chief, and still bestowed saddle, horse, vessels, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder made him cavalry chief and gave him horse and gear.

sentences.zh: 及佐朱珍討時溥，寨於豐、蕭之間，歸厚乘徐壘如行坦途，甚為諸將歎伏。

translations.literal: When aiding Zhu Zhen against Shi Pu he stockaded between Feng and Xiao; Guihou crossed Xu ramparts as if on level road—generals deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Shi Pu he crossed Xu walls as if on flat ground.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，奏遷檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was memorialized transferred honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Longji he became honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，復伐徐，歸厚以偏師徑進，至九里山下與徐兵遇。

translations.literal: That winter he again attacked Xu; Guihou with a separate column went straight forward to below Jiuli Mountain and met Xu troops.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he advanced to Jiuli Mountain against Xu.

sentences.zh: 時我之叛將陳璠在賊陣中，歸厚忽見之，因瞋目大罵，單馬直往，期於必取，會飛矢中左目而退；

translations.literal: At that time our rebel Chen Fan was in the bandit formation; Guihou suddenly saw him, glared and loudly cursed, single horse went straight there intending surely to take him; a flying arrow struck the left eye and he withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing rebel Chen Fan he charged alone until an arrow blinded his left eye;

sentences.zh: 徐戎甚眾，莫敢追之。

translations.literal: Xu troops were very many; none dared pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Xu troops dared not pursue.

sentences.zh: 大順元年，奏加檢校兵部尚書，又命統親軍。

translations.literal: In Datong year 1 he was memorialized added honorary Minister of War and ordered to command the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Datong 1 he became honorary Minister of War and commanded the guard.

sentences.zh: 是歲，郴王遷寨，未知所往，忽逢兗、鄆賊寇甚眾，太祖亟登道左高阜以觀之，命歸厚領所部廳子馬直突之。

translations.literal: That year Prince of Chen moved stockade, destination unknown; suddenly meeting Yan and Yanzhou bandits very many, the Founder urgently climbed a high mound by the road to observe and ordered Guihou to lead his hall-son horse to charge straight in.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan raiders swarmed he charged with the hall-son horse at the Founder's order.

sentences.zh: 出沒二十餘合，賊大敗將北，而救軍雲至，歸厚即綴賊苦戰，請太祖以數十騎先還。

translations.literal: Emerging and withdrawing more than twenty rounds, bandits were greatly defeated and about to flee north, but rescue troops clouded in; Guihou then fought the bandits bitterly and begged the Founder with several tens of horse to return first.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty clashes he held the enemy while the Founder escaped with a few horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時歸厚所乘馬中流矢而踣，乃持槊步鬥漸退，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: At that time Guihou's mounted horse was struck by a flowing arrow and fell; he then held his spear and fought on foot gradually retreating; bandits did not dare press.
translations.idiomatic: His horse fell; he fought on foot with his spear until the enemy dared not close.

sentences.zh: 太祖至寨，亟命張筠、劉儒飛騎來迎，然謂已歿矣。

translations.literal: The Founder reached camp and urgently ordered Zhang Yun and Liu Ru with flying horse to welcome; yet he thought him already dead.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Zhang Yun and Liu Ru to find him, fearing him dead.

sentences.zh: 歸厚體被二十餘箭，尚復拒戰，筠等既至，賊解乃歸。

translations.literal: Guihou's body received more than twenty arrows yet still resisted battle; when Yun and the rest arrived bandits dispersed and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded by twenty arrows he fought until Yun arrived and the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 太祖見之，撫背泣下曰：「 得歸厚身全，縱廣喪戎馬，何足計乎！

translations.literal: The Founder seeing him stroked his back and wept, saying: "To get Guihou's body whole—even if broadly losing army horses, what is worth counting!"
translations.idiomatic: The Founder wept with joy: "Your life is worth any number of horses!"

sentences.zh: 」便令肩舁歸汴，日降問賚，恩旨甚厚，尋遷中軍指揮使。

translations.literal: He then ordered him carried on shoulders back to Bian; daily descending inquiries and gifts; imperial favor very thick; soon he was transferred central army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Carried to Bian he was richly honored and made central army commander.

sentences.zh: 景福初，從太祖伐鄆，帝軍不利，太祖為寇所逼，歸厚殿馬翼衛，左右馳射，矢發如雨，賊騎千百，披靡而退。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu following the Founder in attacking Yan the imperial army was unfavorable; the Founder was pressed by bandits; Guihou brought up the rear wing-guarding, left and right galloping and shooting; arrows fell like rain; bandit cavalry by thousands and hundreds collapsed and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfu he covered the Founder's retreat with arrow storms at Yan.

sentences.zh: 明年，與葛從周禦晉軍於洹水，殊績尤著。

translations.literal: The next year with Ge Congzhou he met Jin troops at Huan River; special merit was especially marked.
translations.idiomatic: Next year at Huan River his merit was outstanding.

sentences.zh: 詔加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: An edict added honorary Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He became honorary Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 其後，討滄州，復洺州，咸以功聞，太祖錄其勳，命權知洺州事。

translations.literal: Afterward attacking Cangzhou and recovering Ming prefecture—all with merit reported—the Founder recorded his merit and ordered him provisional Ming prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Cang and Ming campaigns he governed Ming provisionally.

sentences.zh: 是郡嘗兩為晉人所陷，井邑蕭條，歸厚撫之，數月之內，民庶翕然。

translations.literal: This prefecture had twice been taken by Jin men; towns and hamlets were desolate; Guihou comforted it; within months the people were harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He restored desolate Ming within months.

sentences.zh: 太祖自鎮、定還，睹其緝理之政，大喜，賞之。

translations.literal: The Founder returning from Zhen and Ding saw his governing policy and was greatly pleased and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder praised his governance on return from Zhen and Ding.

sentences.zh: 天復元年冬，真拜洺州刺史，加檢校左僕射，尋授絳州刺史。

translations.literal: In winter of Tianfu year 1 he was formally made Ming prefecture military commissioner, added honorary Left Vice Director; soon appointed Jiang prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 1 winter he became Ming then Jiang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，改晉州刺史，仍檢校司空。

translations.literal: In autumn of year 3 he was changed Jin prefecture military commissioner, still honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3 autumn he became Jin commissioner and honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 唐帝遷都洛陽，除右神武統軍。

translations.literal: When Tang emperor moved the capital to Luoyang he was made Right Divine Martial overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Luoyang he commanded Right Divine Martial.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年，改左羽林統軍，與徐懷玉同守澤州。

translations.literal: In Tianyou year 2 he was changed Left Feathered Forest overall commander and with Xu Huaiyu jointly guarded Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 2 he guarded Ze with Xu Huaiyu.

sentences.zh: 時晉軍五萬來攻，郡中戎士甚寡，歸厚極力拒守，並軍乃還。

translations.literal: At that time fifty thousand Jin troops came to attack; warriors in the prefecture were very few; Guihou exhausted strength holding fast and Jin army then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He held Ze against fifty thousand Jin until they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was added honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication he became honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 開平二年夏，劉知俊以同州叛，歸厚副楊師厚、劉鄩等討平之。

translations.literal: In summer of Kaiping year 2 Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou; Guihou as deputy to Yang Shihou and Liu Ye and others suppressed and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiping 2 summer he helped suppress Liu Zhijun at Tong.

sentences.zh: 秋，軍還，授亳州團練使。

translations.literal: In autumn the army returned; he was appointed Bozhou training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn he became Bozhou training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年，拜鎮國軍節度使、陝虢等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In Qianhua year 2 he was made Zhenguo military commissioner and Shan-Guo surveillance and disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Qianhua 2 he became Zhenguo and Shan-Guo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，以疾卒於位。

translations.literal: The next summer he died of illness in office.
translations.idiomatic: Next summer he died in office.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太師。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子漢卿。

translations.literal: Son Hanqing.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hanqing.

sentences.zh: 張歸弁，字從冕。

translations.literal: Zhang Guibian, style name Congmian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guibian, styled Congmian.

sentences.zh: 始與兄歸霸、歸厚同歸於太祖，得署為牙校。

translations.literal: At first with brothers Guiba and Guihou he together returned to the Founder and was appointed guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered with Guiba and Guihou as guard officer.

sentences.zh: 時太祖初鎮宣武，屢命歸弁結好於近境，頗得行人之儀。

translations.literal: When the Founder first held Xuanyi, he repeatedly ordered Guibian to knit good relations with near borders, quite obtaining travelers' courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He handled frontier diplomacy for the early Xuanyi command.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，以偏師佐葛從周禦並軍於洹水。

translations.literal: In Qianning he with a separate column aided Ge Congzhou in meeting Jin troops at Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Qianning he aided Congzhou at Huan River.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，又佐張存敬與燕人戰於內黃，積前後功，表授檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: In Guangqi he again aided Zhang Cunjing in fighting Yan men at Neihuang; accumulating former and later merit he was memorialized honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi at Neihuang he became honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 大順初，攻討兗、鄆，命歸弁佐衡王友諒屯單父，軍聲大振，尋為齊州指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong attacking Yan and Yanzhou he was ordered to aid Prince of Heng Youliang to camp at Shanfu; military prestige greatly shook; soon he was Qi prefecture commander.
translations.idiomatic: Datong at Yan he camped at Shanfu with Youliang and became Qi commander.

sentences.zh: 屬青帥王師範叛，遣將詐為賈人，挽車數十乘，匿兵器於其中，將謀竊發，歸弁察而擒之，州城以寧。

translations.literal: When Qing commander Wang Shifan rebelled he sent generals feigning merchants, several tens of carts, hiding weapons within, intending to steal a sudden outbreak; Guibian detected and captured them; the prefectural city was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He foiled Wang Shifan's merchants smuggling arms into Qi.

sentences.zh: 明年春，青寇大舉來伐，州兵既寡，民意頗搖，有本郡都將。

translations.literal: The next spring Qing raiders came in great force to attack; prefectural troops were few and popular hearts somewhat shaken; there were native-command officers.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring Qing attacked; the city wavered when officers plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 康文爽等三人欲謀外應，即時擒獲誅之，人心遂定。

translations.literal: Kang Wenshuang and three others wished to plot outer response; he at once captured and executed them; popular hearts were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Kang Wenshuang and three conspirators.

sentences.zh: 歸弁又罄發私帑，賞給士伍，青州平，超加檢校右僕射，遙領愛州刺史。

translations.literal: Guibian also exhausted his private stores to reward and give to soldiers; Qing was pacified; he was specially added honorary Right Vice Director, holding Ai prefecture military commission at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his own treasury on the troops; after Qing fell he became honorary Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 從征荊、襄回，轉檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: Returning from campaigning in Jing and Xiang he was transferred honorary Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing and Xiang he became honorary Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年春，太祖入魏誅牙軍，魏之郡邑多叛，歸弁與諸將等分布攻討，封境悉平。

translations.literal: In spring of Tianyou year 3 the Founder entered Wei and executed the guard army; Wei's prefectures and districts mostly rebelled; Guibian with generals and others separately distributed attack and suppression; the sealed borders were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 3 spring he helped pacify Wei after the guard massacre.

sentences.zh: 而歸弁於高唐攻賊太猛，飛矢中於臆，太祖嘉之，命賜鞍勒馬一匹、金帶一條。

translations.literal: Yet Guibian at Gaotang attacked bandits too fiercely; a flying arrow struck his chest; the Founder praised it and ordered bestowed one saddle, bridle, and horse, one gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded storming Gaotang he won a horse and gold belt from the Founder.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，命權知晉州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer he was ordered provisional Jin prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Summer month 5 he acted as Jin commissioner.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，真授晉州刺史，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter he was formally appointed Jin prefecture military commissioner, added honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Winter month 11 he became Jin commissioner and honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，改滑州長劍指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was changed Huazhou long-sword commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication he commanded Huazhou long-sword troops.

sentences.zh: 開平二年秋九月，並軍圍平陽，詔歸弁統兵救之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn of Kaiping year 2 Jin troops besieged Pingyang; an edict ordered Guibian to lead troops to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiping 2 autumn he relieved besieged Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 軍至，解其圍，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When the army arrived it lifted the encirclement; he was added honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the siege and became honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三年春三月，寢疾，卒於滑州之私第。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring of year 3 he fell ill in bed and died at his private residence in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3 spring he died at his Huazhou home.

sentences.zh: 子漢融。

translations.literal: Son Hanrong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hanrong.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：從周以驍武之才，事雄猜之主，而能取功名於馬上，啟手足於牖下，靜而言之，斯為賢矣！

translations.literal: The historian says: Congzhou with fierce martial talent served a heroically suspicious lord, yet could take fame and achievement on horseback and open hands and feet below the window—in calm speech, this is worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The historian praises Congzhou for serving a suspicious lord yet dying in honor.

sentences.zh: 彥章蔚有將才，死於讒口，身既歿矣，國亦隨之，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yanzhang had abundant general talent yet died at slander's mouth; body already perished, state also followed—pity!
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang's murder doomed the state—pity!

sentences.zh: 歸霸昆仲，皆脫身於巨盜之流，宣力於興王之運。

translations.literal: The Guiba brothers all escaped from great bandit streams and displayed strength in the rising-king's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang brothers left banditry to build the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 由介胄而析圭爵，可不謂壯夫歟！

translations.literal: From armor and helmet to split tallies and ranks—can they not be called stalwart men!
translations.idiomatic: From soldiers to nobles—they were true stalwarts!
